MDCAT Aggregate Calculator

This MDCAT aggregate calculator works out your merit aggregate exactly the way admissions do: 10% Matric, 40% FSc and 50% MDCAT. Enter obtained and total marks for each and see your aggregate percentage instantly.

🔒 Your files never leave your device.

How to use

  1. Enter your Matric obtained and total marks.
  2. Enter your FSc obtained and total marks, then your MDCAT marks.
  3. Press Calculate aggregate to see your merit percentage and each part's contribution.

How it works

Aggregate = (Matric % × 10%) + (FSc % × 40%) + (MDCAT % × 50%). Each exam is first converted to a percentage, then weighted. Because MDCAT carries half the total weight, a small MDCAT improvement moves the aggregate more than the same improvement in Matric.

Worked example: Example: Matric 900/1100 (81.82%), FSc 950/1100 (86.36%), MDCAT 170/200 (85%) gives 8.18 + 34.55 + 42.50 = 85.23% aggregate.

Frequently asked questions

What is the MDCAT aggregate formula?

Matric counts 10%, FSc counts 40% and MDCAT counts 50%. Each is taken as a percentage of its total marks before weighting.

How much MDCAT score do I need for a good aggregate?

It depends on your Matric and FSc marks, but because MDCAT is 50% of the aggregate, most students need 85% or above in MDCAT to stay competitive for public-sector colleges.

Does this calculator work for all provinces?

The 10/40/50 weighting is the standard formula used for MDCAT admissions across Pakistan. Always confirm the current year's policy with the admitting university.

Can I use marks from improvement exams?

Yes — enter whichever final marks appear on your result cards; the formula is the same.
